digest.headline: The Nasdaq recorded its worst session in four months as US tech stocks fell and oil prices touched $117.

lede.b: The Nasdaq is a US stock market index, which is a collection of shares grouped together to measure the performance of a sector. It suffered its worst session in four months during the latest trading. Strong company earnings collided with AI bubble fears and oil prices touching $117. Two-thirds of S&P 500 stocks gained, but the headline index still fell. Realty Income shares climbed back as Treasury yields retreated from earlier levels.
lede.i: The Nasdaq recorded its worst session in four months as strong corporate earnings collided with artificial intelligence bubble concerns and oil touching $117. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 both slipped lower during the session. Index concentration masked positive breadth across smaller constituents, with two-thirds of S&P 500 stocks actually gaining ground. Realty Income shares advanced as Treasury yields retreated from their earlier intraday peaks.
lede.a: The Nasdaq printed its worst session in four months as robust earnings collided with artificial intelligence valuation concerns and crude touching $117. Index concentration heavily masked positive breadth across smaller constituents, with two-thirds of S&P 500 stocks advancing on the day. Realty Income shares recovered as Treasury yields pulled back from session highs.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: US indices slip as tech stocks drop and oil rises

stories.b: The Nasdaq is an index, which is a list of tech stocks grouped together to track how the market is doing. It just had its worst day in 4 months. The S&P 500 is another big group of US companies. It slipped alongside the Nasdaq on Thursday.
stories.i: The Nasdaq recorded its worst session in 4 months during the latest trading. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 both slipped lower. Strong earnings collided with AI bubble fears and oil prices touching $117.
stories.a: The Nasdaq suffered its worst single-day performance in 4 months alongside a pullback in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100. Equity prices retreated as robust corporate earnings met rising artificial intelligence valuation concerns and crude oil reaching $117 per barrel.

stories.t: Index Breadth Diverges as Treasury Yields Ease
stories.b: Two-thirds of the stocks in the S&P 500 actually went up on Thursday. However, the overall index still fell because a few giant companies dropped. Meanwhile, Treasury yields, which are the interest rates the government pays to borrow money, went down, helping Realty Income stock climb back up.
stories.i: Two-thirds of S&P 500 stocks gained on Thursday, but the headline index still fell. Realty Income shares climbed back as Treasury yields retreated from earlier levels. Index concentration masked positive breadth across smaller constituents.
stories.a: Market breadth diverged as two-thirds of S&P 500 constituents advanced despite a headline index decline. Realty Income recovered ground as Treasury yields retreated, though broader macroeconomic challenges persisted.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Insurers insure robots and bond yields revive trades

stories.t: Tokio Marine offers coverage for artificial intelligence robots
stories.b: Tokio Marine is the first Japanese nonlife insurer to cover AI-enabled robots. This means the company pays for damages or accidents caused by machines that think for themselves. Artificial intelligence helps these machines make their own choices.
stories.i: Tokio Marine introduces the first nonlife insurance policy in Japan covering AI-enabled robots. The firm structured this product to underwrite the operational risks of autonomous systems. Commercial deployment of smart machinery expands as specialized underwriting evolves.
stories.a: Tokio Marine establishes the domestic nonlife sector's initial underwriting framework for autonomous robotic systems. This product launch shifts liability pricing for machine learning integration in commercial settings. Insurers must now model tail risks for algorithmic decision-making without historical loss data.

stories.t: Japanese bond yields draw attention to currency borrowing strategies
stories.b: Japanese bond yields put Bitcoin back in the yen carry trade crosshairs. Yields are the money a government pays investors who lend to it, like interest on a loan. Traders borrow cheap money in Japan to buy higher-returning assets elsewhere.
stories.i: Japan's sovereign bond yields reintroduce digital assets into the yen carry trade calculus. Investors borrow low-yielding Japanese currency to fund leveraged positions in higher-beta assets. Shifting local yields alter the funding cost dynamics for these cross-border macro positions.
stories.a: Japanese debt yields alter the funding leg of the yen carry trade, drawing speculative crypto flows back into focus. Macro funds monitor the spread between local debt returns and offshore risk assets to gauge liquidation pressures. Tightening domestic monetary conditions threaten the profitability of leveraged arbitrage strategies funded in yen.

politics.b: Japan's defense academy chief called for three red lines against China. A net provider named GMO asked the government for active cyber defense. A data leak victim at Park24 will receive three thousand yen.
politics.i: The Japan defense academy chief demanded three red lines regarding China. Internet provider GMO urged the government to implement active cyber defense measures. Park24 agreed to pay three thousand yen to individuals affected by a data leak.
politics.a: The defense academy commandant articulated three red lines concerning China. Concurrently, network operator GMO petitioned state authorities for active cyber defense capabilities. Data leak victims at Park24 are slated to receive three thousand yen each.

India.label: India
India.sub: Rupee defences and Nifty index movements

stories.t: Central bank steps on currency value
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India stepped in to protect the local currency. Analysts called these moves short-term fixers. A currency is like the official money of a country used for trade. The central bank acts as the main money manager for the nation.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India deployed measures viewed by observers as temporary carry trade dampeners and stabilisers. The central bank's interventions aimed to support the rupee against depreciation pressures. Market participants evaluated these actions as short-term fixes rather than structural solutions for the exchange rate.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India deployed interventions that analysts classified as short-term stabilisers rather than durable policy pivots. These measures targeted speculative carry dynamics without altering the fundamental macroeconomic balance. Traders adjusted their positioning as the central bank absorbed immediate volatility in the foreign exchange market.

stories.b: The Nifty stock index recorded its third-longest price drop in history. This downward move was also the shallowest drop ever seen for the index. A stock index tracks the combined value of many companies to show how the market is doing.
stories.i: The Nifty benchmark logged its third-longest technical correction on record. Market data showed this downward phase was the shallowest in the history of the index. Investors assessed their equity mutual fund portfolios during this market correction.
stories.a: The Nifty recorded its third-longest technical correction while registering as the shallowest drawdown in its historical series. Market participants evaluated equity mutual fund exposures amid this protracted consolidation phase. Price action across major benchmarks demonstrated compressed volatility relative to prior historical corrections.

stories.b: The Houthis carried out seven operations against Saudi airports and energy sites. Riyadh reported missile interceptions following these events. A massive fire broke out at an Aramco oil facility in Riyadh. Air India kept its flights to Riyadh and Dammam suspended.
stories.i: The Houthis targeted Saudi airports and energy sites across seven separate operations. Riyadh confirmed that missile interceptions occurred during the strikes. An Aramco facility in Riyadh suffered a massive fire. Air India maintained the suspension of its Riyadh and Dammam routes.

A massive fire erupted at an Aramco facility in the capital. Air India extended flight suspensions to Riyadh and Dammam.

stories.t: Crude Output Recovers as OPEC Cuts Demand Forecast
stories.b: Saudi Arabia reported a crude output recovery from a 30-year low. This follows recent production constraints. Meanwhile, OPEC halved its 2026 demand growth forecast. The International Monetary Fund stated that the economic impact of the recent attacks is limited for now.
stories.i: Saudi Arabia reported a crude output recovery from a 30-year low. OPEC halved its 2026 demand growth forecast at the same time. The International Monetary Fund assessed that the economic impact of the recent attacks remains limited for now.
stories.a: Saudi Arabia announced a crude output recovery from a 30-year low. OPEC simultaneously halved its 2026 demand growth forecast. The International Monetary Fund noted that the macroeconomic impact of the recent attacks is limited for now.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Naira falls as trading volume hits $1.01 billion

stories.t: Naira Slips in Official Market Sessions
stories.src: The Rio Times · MarketForces Africa · Tribune Online
stories.b: The official Nigerian currency, called the naira, lost 2.1% of its value in a single day. It traded at 1,395 naira to one United States dollar. Total trading volume reached $1.01 billion.
stories.i: The naira declined by 2.1% against the dollar in a single trading session. Currency exchange rates settled at 1,395 naira per dollar as order book activity intensified. Total foreign exchange trading volume reached $1.01 billion.
stories.a: The naira depreciated by 2.1% to print at 1,395 against the dollar amid surging foreign exchange order book depth. Aggregate turnover touched $1.01 billion across the trading session, reflecting heightened liquidity demands. Official market quotes adjusted downward by 17 naira per dollar.

stories.t: Foreign Reserves Climb While Flutterwave Expands Corridors
stories.b: Nigeria's foreign reserves grew to $55.16 billion. Payment company Flutterwave connected 300 Chinese suppliers to a direct naira payment system for imports. Trade participants can now use this corridor.
stories.i: Nigerian foreign reserves expanded to $55.16 billion. Payment firm Flutterwave integrated 300 Chinese suppliers into a direct naira payment corridor. Import traders utilize this system to settle transactions.
stories.a: External reserves scaled to $55.16 billion, providing a wider buffer for monetary authorities. Flutterwave onboarded 300 Chinese suppliers onto a bilateral payment channel designed for direct naira settlement of import trade. This infrastructure alters the invoicing mechanics for participating import desks.

politics.b: President Tinubu started his re-election campaign as economic hardship tests public support. Officials in Kaduna dismissed rumors about a 2.3 trillion naira campaign budget. Political figures urged the administration to fix internal issues before the 2027 vote.
politics.i: President Tinubu launched his re-election campaign amid economic pressures. The Kaduna state government refuted claims regarding a 2.3 trillion naira campaign allocation. Political stakeholders urged executive restructuring ahead of the 2027 elections.
politics.a: President Tinubu initiated his 2027 re-election bid against a backdrop of macroeconomic strain. Kaduna state authorities publicly rejected fabricated reports citing a 2.3 trillion naira ruling party campaign fund. Public figures publicly conditioned future electoral success on executive administrative remediation.
